title: Practical theorems 1–5
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 3. No creature but God alone stands as toward be religiously adored. 4. Even when we distinctly invoke Father, Son, and Spirit, one God stands as adored. 5. Spiritual goods stand as toward be sought without condition insofar as they concern God's glory and salvation; temporal goods with ye condition if God wills. — XIV. Corollaries: 1. Prayers should be born in ye heart and formed with ye mouth. 2. Christians stand as invited toward continual prayer by command, promises, and needs.
pass_b_english: XIV. Corollaries: 1. Prayers should be born in the heart and formed with the mouth. 2. Christians are invited to continual prayer by command, promises, and needs.

3. No creature but God alone is to be religiously adored. 4. Even when we distinctly invoke Father, Son, and Spirit, one God is adored. 5. Spiritual goods are to be sought without condition insofar as they concern God's glory and salvation; temporal goods with the condition if God wills.
source_text: XIV. Consectaria: 1. Preces in corde nasci, ore vero formari debent. 2. Christiani ad assidue orandum invitantur mandato, promissionibus, necessitatibus. 3. Nulla creatura sed solus Deus religiose adorandus est. 4. Etiamsi distincte Patrem, Filium, Spiritum invocamus, unus Deus adoratur. 5. Bona spiritualia petenda sine conditione quatenus ad Dei gloriam et salutem pertinent; temporalia cum conditione si Deo visum.
